headline: Strong volumes; GAAP results skewed by a settlement gain
summary_short: Net operating revenues rose 6.8% y/y to $5,628M in Q2 FY2026 on higher hospital and ambulatory volumes. GAAP diluted EPS of $9.84 includes a $413M one-time gain from the early conclusion of the Conifer-CHI revenue cycle agreement, while Adjusted EBITDA — which excludes that gain — rose a cleaner 16.3% y/y to $1,304M.
summary_long: Hospital Operations revenue rose 6.0% y/y on higher patient volumes, partly offset by a less favorable payer mix; Ambulatory Care rose 9.3% on 2025-2026 acquisitions, de novo development, and commercial rate increases. GAAP operating income and net income include a $413 million one-time gain from the early conclusion of the Conifer-CHI revenue cycle agreement; segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes it, still grew 16.3% y/y to $1.304 billion. The company guides FY2026 capital expenditures to $700-$800 million. Cash fell to $2.170 billion from $2.967 billion at March 31, 2026 after $1.042 billion of share repurchases and a $558 million Conifer noncontrolling-interest purchase; shareholders' equity rose 24.3% y/y to $4.658 billion.

drivers.explanation: Higher patient volumes across both segments plus a $413M one-time revenue-cycle settlement gain drove strong reported growth; segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes that gain, still rose 16.3% y/y on volume and cost discipline. The 10-Q guides FY2026 capex to $700-$800 million.

Hospital Operations revenue +6.0% y/y on higher patient volumes, partly offset by a less favorable payer mix; Ambulatory Care +9.3% on 2025-2026 acquisitions/de novo development plus commercial rate increases and higher patient acuity.

Includes a $413 million one-time gain from the early conclusion of the Conifer-CHI revenue cycle agreement (Omnibus Agreement); segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes this gain, rose a smaller 16.3% y/y.
Follows the operating-income gain from the one-time settlement; income tax expense scaled with higher pretax income. Not explained further in the release.
213% y/y growth combines the one-time settlement gain in net income with an 8.5% smaller weighted diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.

This segment-level non-GAAP measure excludes the $413M contract-termination gain; its 16.3% y/y rise reflects the same hospital-volume and ambulatory-growth drivers cited above, without the one-time boost.
This third-party EBITDA proxy is built from GAAP operating income and therefore also includes the $413M one-time settlement gain; not comparable to the company's own Adjusted EBITDA figure above.

Cash fell from $2.967 billion at March 31, 2026 mainly on $1.042 billion of share repurchases, $558 million to purchase noncontrolling interests in Conifer, and $341 million of interest payments in the quarter.
Growth reflects six-month net income of $1.528 billion plus an additional-paid-in-capital increase from the Conifer noncontrolling-interest redemption, partly offset by treasury-stock repurchases.
Reflects ongoing share repurchases under the buyback program; 7.021 million shares were repurchased in the six months ended June 30, 2026.
